question_type: two-month percent difference of a monthly 'total' series; component-vs-summary table choice plus an ambiguous percent-difference formula
decisive_step: Two choices. (1) Source: the broadest expenditure total is the 'Expenditures > Total' column of 'Summary of Federal Receipts and Expenditures' (1939_02:232 / 1939_03:183 / 1939_04:188; identical in every 1939 printing), not the Total column of the component table 'Federal Expenditures - General' (1939_02:265 etc.), and not the later, differently based monthly budget series in 1940-1948 issues. The reference made this choice (solution.structured.json key_sources: 1939_03:193 and :204; review.md check 4 explicitly rejects the 'General' subtotal). (2) Formula: the grader accepted cell a's symmetric percent difference (|A-B| over the mean of A and B); the reference, with the same source cells, used percent change relative to the earlier month (review.md check 5, calc.py 'pct_change') and is graded wrong. Only a got both choices right.

smallest_change.change: Component-of cross-reference in show_table NOTES and find_tables group lines. otables already computes within-table identities (e.g. 'c8 = sum c9..c13'); add a same-issue, same-section pass that matches each table's first value column ('Total') against the value columns of the other tables (equal on >=80% of >=5 shared periods). When it matches a non-Total column of a table that also has a broader 'Total' column, print under NOTES of the component table: `  - c1 'Total' of this table = c9 'Expenditures 2/ > General' of TABLE 'Summary of Federal Receipts and Expenditures' (treasury_bulletin_1939_02.txt:232), which also has c8 'Expenditures 2/ > Total' (= General + Recovery and relief + Revolving funds + Transfers to trust accounts): for 'total' questions use that column`; and in find_tables: `[-] Federal Expenditures - General | 4 issues 1939_01..1939_04 | match:title | component of: Summary of Federal Receipts and Expenditures (col 'Expenditures > General')`. b2 would have seen the NOTE at b2[13] and c at c[11], on the page they were reading.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: the note is additive and prints only when a numeric column identity holds across two tables of the same issue; a right cell that already picked the summary table sees nothing new. c would also need the formula fix (alternative 1); b never opened a 1939 table.

alternatives.change: Add: 'Percent difference vs percent change: "percent difference between A and B" (no direction given) = |A-B| / ((A+B)/2) x 100; "percent change / increase from A to B" = (B-A) / A x 100. Print both with calc and pick by the wording.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Fixes only the formula (c, and b's formula), and the convention is unverified: the reference solver called relative-to-earlier 'standard in this benchmark' (review.md check 1) and is graded wrong here, while a's symmetric value is graded right. Check the other percent-difference questions in the 50 before adopting; could flip right cells elsewhere if the grader is inconsistent.

Offer: <recomputed>'.

fix.why_not_text: b2 had the identical AGENTS.md as a, at temperature 0, and still committed to the 'General' table at b2[9], as did c at c[9]; only a re-queried (a[19]-[21]). The relevant sentence exists and was followed by 1 of 3 text cells. A NOTE printed on the table page the model is already reading (b2[13], c[11]) is seen with certainty; whether it is acted on is the residual risk (hence medium confidence). The formula convention is the one part where text is the natural lever, but its correctness across the benchmark is unverified (alternative 1).
fix.irreducible: Partly. The formula is a coin flip even with the right table: the reference solver picked the same source as a and the opposite formula and is graded wrong; the wording ('absolute percent difference ... rounded ... in millions of dollars') is muddled. Not disputed (issue47 false), but a cell that gets the source right still needs the symmetric convention.

notes: (1) OCR header shift: in the 1939_01 Summary printing the column labels are offset by one, so printings lists the Total value under the 'Recovery and relief' label (a[30]) and its SUMMARY reports the Total as 2 printings instead of 3 plus a spurious extra column; the reference solver fixed this by hand via component sums (review.md check 2). A column-identity relabel inside printings would remove it. (2) find_tables ranking: for 'Federal expenditures' the four 'Federal Expenditures - ...' component tables (match:title) fill the first 8000 bytes and the Summary table (match:tokens) is cut (b2[8], c[8]); a only saw it after adding 'total' to the query. Rank a same-section summary table with its components, or print components indented under their summary. (3) a[18]: printings printed nothing for the Jan-1939 General row while b2[15] got 3 printings from the same command; intermittent empty output worth checking in the tool log. (4) 'reported in February 1938': the corpus has no 1938 issues (b[34]), so 'reported in' must mean the data month; b spent 5 steps on this, a/b2/c did not question it. (5) The gate cannot see a table-choice error, and b's three-variant calc without --alt gave competing_candidates nothing; a control that treats every value printed by the final calc as a candidate would at least have surfaced the symmetric variant to b (still the wrong source). (6) --grep matches norm(label) / norm(period) / norm(section) (otables.py:1984); a[10] and b2[11] each lost a step to the 'YYYY-Mon' spelling.
